messages.author: bb17d830c050dbf9
messages.subject: DIVA+J better than DEC+J
parts:
Hi Nick

I´m working with Caribbean anoles, and I´ve used constrained analyisis. I found that DIVA+J model have lower AIC values than DEC+J model. There some species circumnstances when this occurs? 

thanks in advance

Julián

messages.author: 17908c3cf4600a9a
messages.subject: RE:[BioGeoBEARS] DIVA+J better than DEC+J
parts:
Hi,

I had the same pattern with my dataset and I asked the question to Nick.

Here is his answer:

"the subset sympatry parameter implemented in the DEC but not in the DIVAlike model, might not be required to explain the data. As a consequence, the likelihood of the model inflates because the probabilities spread out over more inheritance scenarios "

Hope it helps.

Julien

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] DIVA+J better than DEC+J
parts: Hi! Yeah, that's the answer. Eg if you have lots of sister species with A,AB , that will favor DEC models over DIVALIKE models, whereas lots of AB,CD sisters will favor DIVALIKE models.  If +J is the most important thing then DEC+J and DIVALIKE+J will be similar although one or the other might be a bit better. Cheers! Nick
